passage:
Thomas waited until the end of his one-to-one with Rukmini, in the glass cabin overlooking the Chennai IT corridor, and then said it plainly.
"I want to be considered for team lead next cycle. What exactly would that take, and by when?"
Rukmini put down her coffee. "I'm glad you asked. Three things. One, you haven't run a client review on your own. Two, your estimates slip; last quarter two tasks overran by a week. Three, I need to see you coaching the new hires, not just fixing their code."
Thomas wrote all three down. "And the timeline?"
"The next cycle closes in September. If these three are clearly there by August, I'll put your name forward."
"Can we check every month?"
"First Friday of each month. Bring what you've done."
Thomas walked out with a page of notes and a slightly racing heart.

qa.q: When does the next cycle close?
qa.a: The next cycle closes in September.

qa.q: What does Thomas's slightly racing heart suggest about how he felt leaving the cabin?
qa.a: He was probably nervous and excited at once, glad to have a clear target but aware the three gaps are real work.

qa.q: What else could Thomas do between the monthly check-ins?
qa.a: He could keep a simple record of each client review, estimate and coaching session, so each monthly review is based on facts rather than memory.

qa.q: How does Thomas's request look from Rukmini's side?
qa.a: Rukmini seems pleased that he asked directly, because it lets her name specific gaps and set a fair, checkable plan instead of guessing what he wants.

grounding: It shows someone asking the manager directly what a promotion needs and by when, the manager naming three gaps, and both agreeing monthly progress reviews.

passage:
"Nandini, do you have ten minutes?"
"Sure, Arnab. Sit."
"I'll be direct. I want the senior designer role. What would you need to see, and when?"
Nandini leaned back. "Good. Most people just hint. Okay. First, your visual work is strong, but you haven't presented to a client alone. Second, you need to own a project start to finish, not just the screens. Third, I'd want to see you give useful feedback to the juniors."
"Client presentation, full project, feedback," Arnab repeated, typing. "By when?"
"Promotion discussions are in March. So by February."
"Could we look at it every month? Just so I'm not guessing."
"Last Thursday of the month. You bring evidence; I'll tell you honestly where you are."
Arnab closed the laptop. "Thank you. I was nervous to ask."
"Asking is half of it," Nandini said.

qa.q: How was Arnab feeling before asking, and how can you tell?
qa.a: Arnab was nervous, as Arnab admits at the end; opening with "I'll be direct" sounds like bracing for the answer.

qa.q: What else could Arnab do to make the monthly reviews more useful?
qa.a: Arnab could bring a short written list of progress on each gap, so Nandini can judge progress quickly and honestly.

qa.q: How does Nandini see Arnab's direct question?
qa.a: Nandini welcomes it, noting most people only hint, and it lets Nandini give clear gaps and a timeline.

grounding: It shows someone asking the manager directly what the promotion would require and by when, hearing three gaps and agreeing monthly progress checks.
